news.title: The Army Just Did Something Extraordinary To Break China’s Rare Earth Monopoly

The Army signed a non-binding term sheet to host a commercial rare earth plant on one of its own bases, under a lease that could run past the year 2100. And the company it chose, REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY), already has a head start on what the Army needs most: turning rare earths into metal outside of China. news.summary: Reports about an oil glut are back in the media, and U.S. diesel just dropped below $6 per gallon. But these signs of normalization have yet to reach the airline industry, where jet fuel prices remain eye-wateringly high and hedging contracts are expiring. It seems not all airlines will survive the winter. Airlines have been among the sectors to feel the most immediate pain from the fallout of the war between the United States and Israel, and Iran. news.title: Uganda Pushes First Oil to Mid-2027 as Iran War Holds Up Equipment

news.summary: The AI boom is pushing developers to test a new frontier for positioning data centers, following the growing backlash against the excessive use of land, water, and energy resources onshore. So hyperscalers and start-ups have moved to test placing data centers under the sea or floating on ships, to save on water, land, and electricity use.
